what_its_for: Evinacumab-Dgnb is used along with other cholesterol-lowering medicines to treat adults and children (12 years and older) who have a condition called Homozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia (HoFH). This is a rare inherited disease that causes very high levels of LDL ('bad') cholesterol in the blood, which can lead to serious heart problems.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion, meaning it goes directly into your vein through a needle or catheter. A doctor, nurse, or other trained healthcare provider will give you this infusion in a clinic or hospital setting. Each infusion takes about 60 minutes. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Do not try to inject it yourself.
dosing: The usual dose is 15 mg per kilogram (mg/kg) of your body weight, given once every 4 weeks (once a month). Your doctor will calculate the exact dose that is right for you based on your weight. Always keep your infusion appointments and do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule your monthly infusion appointment, call your doctor or clinic as soon as possible. Try to reschedule your appointment and then continue on your regular monthly schedule from that new date. Do not try to 'double up' on doses.
storage: You will not store this medicine at home. The healthcare facility where you receive your infusions is responsible for storing Evkeeza. It is stored in a refrigerator at a specific temperature until it is prepared for your infusion. Do not attempt to store or handle the medication yourself.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control (contraception) during treatment and for at least 5 months after the last dose, because this medicine may harm an unborn baby. Avoid becoming pregnant while using this medicine. Breastfeeding is also not recommended during treatment and for 5 months after your last dose. There are no specific foods or drinks to strictly avoid, but continue following any heart-healthy diet your doctor has recommended.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience any signs of a serious allergic reaction during or after your infusion, such as: rash, itching, hives, flushing (redness or warmth), shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, dizziness, lightheadedness, nausea, or a feeling that something is wrong. Also contact your doctor if you feel unwell after any infusion, if you think you might be pregnant, if you are planning to start any new medicines or supplements, or if you have any questions or concerns.
when_it_works: Your LDL ('bad') cholesterol levels may begin to drop within a few weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take several months to see the full benefit. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to check your cholesterol levels and make sure the medicine is working. Keep all of your follow-up appointments even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use if you are pregnant. Use reliable birth control during treatment and for 5 months after your last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for 5 months after stopping. Children: Evkeeza is approved for use in children who are 12 years of age and older. It is not approved for children under 12. Older adults (65+): This medicine can be used in older adults, but always make sure your doctor knows all other medicines you are taking. Kidney or Liver problems: There is currently limited information about the use of this medicine in people with severe kidney or liver disease. Always tell your doctor about any health conditions you have.
